<description>
Return util::Result objects from all functions that can trigger fatal errors.

There are many validation functions that handle failures by calling `AbortNode` and triggering shutdowns, without returning error information to their callers. This makes error handling in libbitcoinkernel application code difficult, because the only way to handle these errors is to register for [notification callbacks](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/src/kernel/notifications_interface.h). Improve this by making all functions that trigger fatal errors return util::Result objects with the error information.

This PR is a pure refactoring that returns extra result information from functions without changing their behavior. It's a possible alternative to and subset of #29642, which adds similar return information but also makes behavior changes and exposes a FatalError type.

---

[2024-07-26] rc:1693183422 inline on src/node/blockstorage.cpp by maflcko (member):
Seems fragile to use `util::Result<InterruptResult>`. Wrapping one result into another is fragile, because call-sites may easily forget to unwrap the inner result, especially if the inner result is otherwise `void`. My recommendation would be to treat interruption as `util::Error`, so that callers don't miss it if they check for errors (but forget to check for interruption), but are free to check it, if they inspect the precise error.
[2024-08-07] rc:1707623223 inline on src/node/blockstorage.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2024-08-07):
re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29700#discussion_r1693183422

[quoted text omitted]
It sounds like you want `Result<InterruptResult, void>` to be replaced with `Result<void, InterruptResult>` which would be ok with me. I don't think the difference between these things is very significant, but I agree maybe if the caller forgets to check for the interrupted status, incorrectly treating the interrupted status like a failure might be safer than incorrectly treating the interrupted status like a success.

[2026-04-01] c:4171045172 comment by purpleKarrot (member) (edited 2026-04-01):
I see Result-style error handling as a rustism that should be kept out of the C++ codebase of Bitcoin core.

It is well known that exceptions in C++ are fast on the happy path but slow on the exceptional path, which makes them unsuitable for systems with hard realtime requirements where time determinism is more important than performance. For such systems, C++23 finally provides a proper error handling mechanism out of the box.

Where does that apply to Bitcoin? Bitcoin's block time is *approximately 10 minutes on average*. That is about as far away from time determinism as anyone can possibly imagine. Instead, all aspects of Bitcoin require runtime performance above all. Miners want to mine faster, nodes want to verify with less power consumption, indexers want to provide faster responses.

Introducing `util::Result` is a development in the wrong direction.

Yes thank you for pointing out this inconsistency. It existed before this PR and this PR doesn't change it but the PR does add a comment and it's better if the comment acknowledges it. Updated in latest push to clarify this comment and related ones.

To describe the issue for others: validation code flushes internally many different places and mostly does not treat flush failures as errors returned to callers. This PR doesn't change that behavior but it does return additional information to callers about whether flushes happened and whether they failed. Most of the validation code that flushes (examples: AcceptToMemoryPool, ConnectTip, ActivateBestChainStep) pass a `state_dummy` variable to the flush code to keep flush errors separate from normal errors. But this code is an exception and passes `state` instead so it's possible for this function to return true even though `state.IsValid()` is false, and for `LoadExternalBlockFile` to fail when it might succeed otherwise. This inconsistency should probably be fixed one way or another, but it's a little outside the scope of this PR so the PR is just adding a comment
